stories.head: IBM previews Granite models with explicit instruction and data boundaries
stories.fact: IBM released experimental Granite 4.1 LLMON previews in 3B and 8B variants. Structured blocks identify instructions, documents and tool results, while an execution block specifies which instruction operates on which inputs.
stories.why: Test document and tool-output injection resistance in MATLAB research assistants; keep execution permissions and risk gates outside the language model.
stories.unc: IBM says boundary-following is learned behavior, not an enforced guarantee. Conventional chat input degrades quality; the bundled template is required.
labels: Documents and tool results: separate blocks
Execution block binds instruction to inputs
stories.credit: IBM Granite model card; released November 12, 2026
stories.alt: Conceptual labels separate trusted instructions from documents and tool results, show execution binding and state that learned boundaries are not a security guarantee.

stories.head: Neural operator-map research quantifies impact-model misspecification
stories.date: Donnelly, Galimberti, Healy and Zhang preprint November 10, 2026
stories.fact: The paper establishes local Lipschitz continuity of an optimal liquidation strategy with respect to model parameters, then builds neural approximations of the solution map and studies costs from misspecifying transient impact.
stories.why: Benchmark a MATLAB execution surrogate against the underlying optimizer and stress unseen impact kernels before using its actions.
stories.unc: The result depends on the modeled execution problem. Approximation accuracy does not establish live fills, universal robustness or profitable trading.
stories.alt: Conceptual labels connect impact parameters with a neural solution map and distinguish optimizer comparison from misspecified-impact stress tests.

stories.head: Friday losses leave U.S. indexes higher for the week
stories.fact: The S&P 500 fell 0.4% Friday to 7,561.67, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.9%. The S&P nevertheless gained 2.5% for the week and the Nasdaq gained 2.3%.
stories.why: Separate daily drawdown from weekly recovery; test breadth and factor leadership before extrapolating an index rebound.
stories.unc: These are rounded completed-session index returns, not SPY/QQQ returns or current executable quotes.
stories.alt: Four labels distinguish Friday S&P and Nasdaq Composite losses from their positive weekly returns, using separate reference periods.

stories.head: October PPI rises 0.3% monthly and 6.5% annually
stories.fact: Final-demand PPI rose 0.3% in October, seasonally adjusted, and 6.5% over twelve months, unadjusted. The index excluding foods, energy and trade services rose 0.5% monthly and 4.9% annually.
stories.why: Preserve each measure and adjustment convention when updating inflation inputs; stress persistent inflation without treating PPI as a Fed decision.
stories.unc: PPI differs from CPI and PCE, and the exclusion measure here also removes trade services. Data are subject to revision.
stories.alt: Labels distinguish monthly and annual final-demand PPI changes and the separate measure excluding food, energy and trade services.

stories.head: Applied Materials reports 53% quarterly revenue growth
stories.date: Applied Materials November 12, 2026; quarter ended October 25
stories.fact: Applied Materials reported fiscal Q4 revenue of $10.41 billion, up 53% year over year, GAAP EPS of $3.40 and non-GAAP EPS of $4.16. Quarterly operating cash flow reached $3.30 billion.
stories.why: Compare semiconductor-equipment demand with margins, cash conversion and customer concentration when evaluating infrastructure exposure.
stories.unc: Non-GAAP figures require reconciliation; one strong quarter does not establish future demand or stock performance.
stories.alt: Separate labels show Applied Materials quarterly revenue and annual growth, GAAP and non-GAAP EPS, and operating cash flow.
